definition: In a careful, thorough way that shows a strong sense of duty to do things right.
example: The club treasurer conscientiously kept a receipt for every purchase, however small.
nuance: Conscientiously means acting with dutiful care, while the look-alike consciously only means acting with awareness or on purpose.
prompt: A lab assistant is recording measurements during a long experiment.
options: She conscientiously logged every reading and double-checked each figure.
He conscientiously made up the missing numbers so he could leave early.
After dozing off at the bench, he woke and was conscientiously alert again.
The assistant conscientiously knocked her coffee over, smearing the notebook.
reasons: Recording and rechecking each result out of responsibility is exactly this kind of care.
Inventing data to save time is the opposite of doing a job faithfully.
This confuses the word with consciously; waking up involves awareness, not a sense of duty.
A clumsy accident shows no deliberate care, so the word does not fit.

practice.prompt: A volunteer is responsible for returning library books to the shelves.
options: He conscientiously checked each call number so no book ended up in the wrong spot.
To finish faster, she conscientiously shoved the books onto any empty shelf.
She didn't conscientiously notice the rain outside until her shift ended.
The old book cart squeaked conscientiously as it rolled down the aisle.
reasons: Taking pains to get every placement right reflects a strong sense of responsibility.
Rushing and ignoring the proper order is neglect, not dutiful effort.
Noticing something is about awareness, so this mixes the word up with consciously.
A cart has no sense of duty, so describing its noise this way ignores the word's meaning.
